name: Omeo Mountain Bike Park

facts.claim: A 114 km network of gravity and cross-country mountain bike trails officially opened on 5 December 2025.
Trails range from family-friendly green trails along Livingstone Creek to double-black gravity descents with up to 590 m of vertical drop.
Trails run through Sam Hill State Forest and Mt Mesley and converge at Livingstone Park, with an asphalt pump track at the trailhead.

ticketUrl_note: No single official park site found; run by East Gippsland Shire Council. Paid shuttles (Blue Dirt, Gravity Dirt) are extras, not entry.
access_note: Riding the trails appears free; uplift shuttles are separate paid extras (Blue Dirt 1-day pass from about AUD 95).
unresolved: Council page does not state explicitly that trail access is free; inferred from shuttles being the only listed charge

name: Corryong

facts.claim: Upper Murray town in north-east Victoria, promoted as the setting of The Man from Snowy River.
Corryong cemetery holds the grave of Jack Riley (1841-1914), the stockman linked to the poem's hero.
The town hosts The Man from Snowy River Bush Festival each April (event, not a spot).

name: Mount Lawson State Park

facts.claim: State park about 70 km east of Albury-Wodonga, between the Murray Valley Highway and the Murray River.
Short and medium-length walking tracks lead to lookouts, waterfalls and rocky creeks.
Mt Lawson Road gives unsealed, fine-weather two-wheel-drive access to most visitor areas.

name: Flinders Street Station

facts.claim: Busiest railway station in Victoria, at Flinders and Swanston streets opposite Federation Square.
The current Federation/Edwardian Baroque building was completed in 1909 to a design by James W. Fawcett.
The 1854 station was the terminus of the first railway in Australia.

name: Queen Victoria Market

facts.claim: Opened in 1878; covers over seven hectares and is billed the largest open-air market in the Southern Hemisphere.
Victorian Heritage Register and National Heritage List site, with an estimated ten million visitors a year.
Official site lists Night Market, tours and Queen's Food Hall.
